Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, producing near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA). Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO with 20.1\% degenerate scores. Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA ($n = 200$)---the largest degradation across all twelve strategies on both datasets. At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.

Self-Consistency produces $\kappa = 0.44$ (Eff-$K = 2.02$). Diverse-Prompt achieves $\kappa = 0.40$ (Eff-$K = 2.21$): prompt variation does not break the underlying correlation. Debate achieves $\kappa = 0.15$ (Eff-$K = 4.44$), nearly tripling the effective sample size, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp. This constitutes a Pareto frontier: methods that increase trace independence destroy accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. content.content: 1	Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces is the dominant test-time aggregation strategy for LLMs, but accuracy gains saturate as sample count grows. The Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) explains this plateau: same-model traces are correlated voters, so additional samples carry diminishing independent information. Symbolic constraints in first-order logic (FOL) appear to offer a way forward, but when extracted by the same model, they inherit the traces' correlation structure. We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}. We study it through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts FOL constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT. Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances and four-seed replication, we find a regime-dependent pattern: positive directional trends ($p < 0.10$ in 2 of 4 seeds, none reaching $p < 0.05$; best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp) occur only in a narrow band around 50--55\% SC baseline on one model and one dataset. Outside this zone, constraints either echo the majority (confirmation bias) or amplify errors. Oracle controls with gold FOL confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound, yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of the oracle ceiling. Twelve remediation strategies (nine prompt-level, three method-level) all fail. Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods reveals a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: methods that increase trace independence collapse accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. The bottleneck is structural: same-model self-extraction cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires.

1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
4	The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
5	SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
6	\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
7	The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.
8	
9	Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this to a degree, but the core limitation persists.
10	Trained reward models \citep{lightman2024prm, wang2024mathshepherd} and diversity-aware sampling \citep{diverseaware2026} break the plateau by injecting external signal, but require trained verifiers or sampling modifications.
11	A more fundamental question remains: can \emph{structured aggregation} over symbolic representations extract information from the same traces that majority voting cannot?
12	
13	Recent neuro-symbolic methods suggest that formal reasoning can complement LLM generation.
14	Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}, LINC \citep{olausson2023linc}, DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, and LogicAgent \citep{luo2025logicagent} each report gains on logical reasoning benchmarks, but introduce components beyond the reasoning model: trained verifiers, solver selection, or external knowledge.
15	A simpler question precedes these extensions: can the \emph{same} model that generates reasoning traces also extract useful formal constraints from them?
16	Self-extraction would be a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model, training data, or external prover.
17	Yet no prior work has systematically evaluated whether self-extracted constraints are useful for aggregation.
18	This motivates our study of Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA): extract FOL constraints from each of $K$ reasoning traces, deduplicate by syntactic equivalence, and select the answer best supported by a weighted partial MAX-SAT solution via Z3 \citep{demoura2008z3} (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
19	
20	We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth as $K$ grows \citep{austensmith1996}.
21	When independence fails, as \citet{ladha1992correlated} show for correlated voters, additional samples carry diminishing information.
22	We measure inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa} and find values from 0.21 to 0.82 across instruction-tuned conditions (0.91 for thinking mode), yielding Eff-$K = 1.20\text{--}3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$ (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}).
23	At Eff-$K \approx 1$, each additional trace is informationally redundant.
24	When the same model both produces traces and extracts constraints, the constraints inherit the traces' biases \citep{huang2024selfcorrect, kambhampati2024position}.
25	We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}: self-extracted constraints cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires for aggregation to surpass SC.
26	\citet{lefort2024condorcet_llm} examine CJT violations in LLM ensembles, but no prior study connects this framework to symbolic constraint extraction.
27	
28	We evaluate SICA across six models (7B--32B), three reasoning domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
29	The central finding is the independence bottleneck; positive directional trends occur only in a narrow region around 50--55\% SC in one model-dataset condition (Mistral-7B on FOLIO, 2 of 4 seeds with $p < 0.10$, none reaching $p < 0.05$; best $+3.43$\,pp).
30	Outside it, confirmation bias renders constraints non-discriminative (Type~A, SC $\geq$ 60\%) or error amplification degrades accuracy (Type~C, SC $\leq$ 40\%).
31	Oracle controls confirm the mechanism is sound: gold FOL yields $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling.
32	Twelve remediation strategies (nine prompt-level, three method-level) all fail, and $\kappa$ generalization reveals a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
33	
34	Our contributions are:
35	\begin{enumerate}
36	\item \textbf{Independence Bottleneck.} Same-model traces yield Fleiss' $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ (Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ for $K = 12$), quantifying why additional traces provide diminishing returns. Oracle controls disambiguate two channels: trace correlation directly limits voting diversity (the SC plateau) and indirectly produces homogeneous constraints causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (\S\ref{sec:condorcet}, \S\ref{sec:effective-k}).
37	
38	\item \textbf{Oracle-Extraction Gap.} Oracle constraints yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$). Self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling, localizing the failure to extraction quality (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).
39	
40	\item \textbf{Regime-Dependent Effect.} Positive trends occur in a narrow band ($\sim$50--55\% SC) in one model on one dataset (best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp, none reaching $p < 0.05$). Three failure modes explain the regime boundaries (\S\ref{sec:main-results}).
41	
42	\item \textbf{Independence-Accuracy Trade-off.} Twelve remediation strategies all fail. Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 (Eff-$K$: $2.0 \to 4.4$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO ($-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA); Diverse-Prompt preserves accuracy but cannot break the correlation floor. 43	\end{enumerate}

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}) constitutes the primary finding of this paper. Diverse-Prompt achieves $\kappa = 0.40$ ($\approx$ SC's $0.44$): prompt variation does not break the correlation. Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. This independence-accuracy trade-off is a fundamental Pareto frontier: methods that increase trace independence necessarily degrade accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. Crucially, this trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results---DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}---each bypass same-model self-extraction, trading simplicity for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal.

\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics. First, $C_0$ (multi-candidate rate) combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling. At Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical for instruction-tuned models at $K = 12$), traces beyond 12 add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method---a result that applies to SC itself, not only to SICA. Together, these diagnostics allow practitioners to determine, before any constraint extraction or trace augmentation, whether additional test-time compute is likely to yield returns.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} No positive SICA effect reaches $p < 0.05$. The four-seed replication yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$. In contrast, negative effects are significant: $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$) and $-2.50$\,pp ($p = 0.011$). Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). The converging evidence rests on the pattern across analyses, not any single $p$-value.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} Our experiments span 7B--32B parameters, but the method-level interventions (ICG, Contrastive, Debate) that test the independence-accuracy trade-off most directly use Mistral-7B. At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting (Debate) may impose cognitive overhead that larger models can absorb. Whether 14B+ or 70B+ models can simultaneously maintain reasoning quality under independence-promoting interventions is an open question. The independence-accuracy trade-off itself is fundamental---it follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs---but the location of the Pareto frontier may shift with scale. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors (data-driven independence), external provers (tool-augmented independence), and multi-model pipelines (ensemble-based independence).

input.old_text: \paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics. \section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

We evaluated Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication. Grounded in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, our analysis explains why SC majority voting saturates and why symbolic constraint aggregation fails to break this plateau under same-model self-extraction at the 7B--14B scale.

The primary finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off. Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods reveals a Pareto frontier: Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 (Eff-$K$: $2.0 \to 4.4$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO ($-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA); methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches, and twelve remediation strategies all fail to escape it.

The independence bottleneck quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: same-model traces produce $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ (Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ at $K = 12$), meaning traces beyond 12 add negligible independent information. Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter, $p < 0.001$); self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling. A directional positive trend ($+3.43$\,pp best, $+1.47$\,pp mean; none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears in one model-dataset condition, but its narrow operating range and seed sensitivity limit practical applicability. For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost diagnostic predicting when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}) constitutes the primary finding of this paper. Diverse-Prompt achieves $\kappa = 0.40$ ($\approx$ SC's $0.44$): prompt variation does not break the correlation. Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. This independence-accuracy trade-off is a fundamental Pareto frontier: methods that increase trace independence necessarily degrade accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. Crucially, this trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results---DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}---each bypass same-model self-extraction, trading simplicity for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal.

\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} No positive SICA effect reaches $p < 0.05$. The four-seed replication yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$. In contrast, negative effects are significant: $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$) and $-2.50$\,pp ($p = 0.011$). Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). The converging evidence rests on the pattern across analyses, not any single $p$-value.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} The method-level interventions that test the trade-off most directly use Mistral-7B. At the 7B scale, Debate may impose cognitive overhead that larger models can absorb; whether 14B+ or 70B+ models shift the Pareto frontier is an open question. The trade-off itself is fundamental---it follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs---but its severity may vary with scale. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.

Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this to a degree, but the core limitation persists.
Trained reward models \citep{lightman2024prm, wang2024mathshepherd} and diversity-aware sampling \citep{diverseaware2026} break the plateau by injecting external signal, but require trained verifiers or sampling modifications.
A more fundamental question remains: can \emph{structured aggregation} over symbolic representations extract information from the same traces that majority voting cannot?

Recent neuro-symbolic methods suggest that formal reasoning can complement LLM generation.
Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}, LINC \citep{olausson2023linc}, DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, and LogicAgent \citep{luo2025logicagent} each report gains on logical reasoning benchmarks, but introduce components beyond the reasoning model: trained verifiers, solver selection, or external knowledge.
A simpler question precedes these extensions: can the \emph{same} model that generates reasoning traces also extract useful formal constraints from them?
Self-extraction would be a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model, training data, or external prover.
Yet no prior work has systematically evaluated whether self-extracted constraints are useful for aggregation.
This motivates our study of Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA): extract FOL constraints from each of $K$ reasoning traces, deduplicate by syntactic equivalence, and select the answer best supported by a weighted partial MAX-SAT solution via Z3 \citep{demoura2008z3} (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).

We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth as $K$ grows \citep{austensmith1996}.
When independence fails, as \citet{ladha1992correlated} show for correlated voters, additional samples carry diminishing information.
We measure inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa} and find values from 0.21 to 0.82 across instruction-tuned conditions (0.91 for thinking mode), yielding Eff-$K = 1.20\text{--}3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$ (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}).
At Eff-$K \approx 2$, traces beyond $K = 12$ add negligible independent information---a scaling ceiling that applies to SC itself, not only to symbolic aggregation.
When the same model both produces traces and extracts constraints, the constraints inherit the traces' biases \citep{huang2024selfcorrect, kambhampati2024position}.
We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}: self-extracted constraints cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires for aggregation to surpass SC.
\citet{lefort2024condorcet_llm} examine CJT violations in LLM ensembles, but no prior study connects this framework to symbolic constraint extraction.

We evaluate SICA across six models (7B--32B), three reasoning domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods shows that Debate reduces inter-trace $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15, tripling Eff-$K$, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches.
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound: gold FOL yields $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling.
Twelve remediation strategies (nine prompt-level, three method-level) all fail.
A directional positive trend occurs in one model-dataset condition (Mistral-7B on FOLIO, 2 of 4 seeds with $p < 0.10$, none reaching $p < 0.05$; best $+3.43$\,pp), but only in a narrow band around 50--55\% SC; outside it, constraints echo the majority (Type~A) or amplify errors (Type~C).
The bottleneck is structural at the 7B--14B scale tested; whether larger models or trained extractors can overcome it remains open.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Independence-Accuracy Trade-off (primary).} Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across three aggregation methods reveals a fundamental Pareto frontier: Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 (Eff-$K$: $2.0 \to 4.4$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO ($-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA); Diverse-Prompt preserves accuracy but cannot break the correlation floor. Twelve remediation strategies (nine prompt-level, three method-level) all fail, confirming that same-model aggregation cannot simultaneously achieve independence and accuracy (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).

\item \textbf{Independence Bottleneck and Diagnostic Tools.} Same-model traces yield Fleiss' $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ (Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ for $K = 12$), quantifying SC's own scaling ceiling: Eff-$K \approx 2$ means traces beyond $K = 12$ add negligible independent information for any aggregation method. The multi-candidate rate $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic predicting when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help (\S\ref{sec:condorcet}, \S\ref{sec:effective-k}).

\item \textbf{Oracle-Extraction Gap.} Oracle constraints yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$). Self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling, localizing the failure to extraction quality, not the symbolic approach (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).

\item \textbf{Regime-Dependent Pattern (directional).} A directional positive trend occurs in a narrow band ($\sim$50--55\% SC) in one model on one dataset (best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp, none reaching $p < 0.05$). Three failure modes---confirmation bias, non-formalizability, error amplification---explain the regime boundaries (\S\ref{sec:main-results}).
\end{enumerate}

Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces is the dominant test-time aggregation strategy for LLMs, but accuracy gains saturate as sample count grows. The Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) explains this plateau: same-model traces are correlated voters, so additional samples carry diminishing independent information. Symbolic constraints in first-order logic (FOL) appear to offer a way forward, but when extracted by the same model, they inherit the traces' correlation structure. We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}. We study it through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts FOL constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT. Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances and four-seed replication, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting. A directional positive trend (best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp; $p < 0.10$ in 2 of 4 seeds, none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears only in one model on one dataset at 50--55\% SC baseline. Oracle controls with gold FOL confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound, yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of the oracle ceiling. The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off revealed by Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods: Debate reduces inter-trace $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15, tripling the effective sample size, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. Methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches. The $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling, and $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic. The bottleneck is structural at the 7B--14B scale tested; whether larger models or trained extractors can overcome it remains open.

4	The regime-dependent pattern in \S\ref{sec:main-results} establishes \emph{where} SICA succeeds and fails. This section investigates \emph{why}: trace correlation quantifies the SC plateau (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}), supporting diagnostics confirm the mechanism (Appendices~\ref{app:extraction}--\ref{app:entropy}), and remediation analysis reveals a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).

Two conditions are jointly necessary for positive $\Delta$: sufficient $K_{\text{eff}}$ (Qwen conditions with $K_{\text{eff}} \leq 1.30$ never improve) and sufficient SC accuracy (Mistral on ProofWriter with the highest $K_{\text{eff}} = 3.62$ but SC $= 39\%$ produces significant degradation). 40	\subsection{Supporting Diagnostic Analyses}
41	
42	Four additional analyses confirm the mechanism underlying SICA's failure. Extraction error taxonomy (Appendix~\ref{app:extraction}): 91.8\% of constraints are technically discriminative, but their discriminative direction mirrors the majority answer; removing the 8.2\% non-discriminative constraints yields zero improvement. Constraint ablation (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}): on Mistral-7B ($n = 804$, FOLIO + ProofWriter pooled), MAX-SAT and count-only agree on 94.4\% of predictions, with disagreements split nearly evenly (18 vs.\ 17); the solver's weighted satisfiability computation adds no value over simple constraint counting because constraint weights carry information redundant with vote counts (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). Per-domain, MAX-SAT provides a marginal edge in the intermediate-SC region (59.3\% vs.\ count-only 56.9\%) but actively hurts in the Type~C regime (36.5\% vs.\ 37.2\%), mirroring the regime-dependent pattern of SICA itself. Hyperparameter sensitivity (Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity}): $K = 12$ is the only setting with $\Delta > 2$\,pp among five $K$ values, and only $T = 0.7$ among four temperatures yields a positive effect; both peaks coincide with relatively low SC baselines rather than reflecting hyperparameter effects per se. Entropy decomposition (Appendix~\ref{app:entropy}): all SICA effects concentrate in high-entropy problems ($\Delta$ up to $+12.8$\,pp in the intermediate-SC region), but the direction depends on the accuracy regime---high entropy signals correctable uncertainty only when the model has partial knowledge.

44	\subsection{Remediation Analysis}
45	\label{sec:remediation}
46	\label{sec:interventions}
47	
48	We test twelve remediation strategies: nine prompt-level spanning six dimensions (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:remediation}) and three method-level (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). All nine prompt-level strategies fail. Contrastive prompting reduces non-discriminative constraints from 8.2\% to 6.0\% but newly discriminative constraints still mirror the majority ($\Delta = -1.1$\,pp). Cross-model extraction fails in both directions: weaker models extracting from stronger traces yield 0\% discriminative constraints; stronger models extracting from weaker traces produce accuracy within $\pm$1\,pp of self-extraction. Only 1 of 4 temperature settings yields a positive effect ($p = 0.092$); multi-temperature sampling produces $\Delta = 0.00$\,pp.
49	
50	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} Three method-level strategies target different aspects of the independence bottleneck on Mistral-7B (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from the problem statement, producing near-zero average effect ($\Delta = -1.96$\,pp and $+1.47$\,pp across two FOLIO seeds; $-0.50$\,pp on LogiQA). Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints for each candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA, with ${\sim}$21\% degenerate scores on both datasets. Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.00$\,pp on LogiQA ($n = 200$)---the largest degradation across all twelve strategies on both datasets. At the 7B scale, multi-role prompting adds cognitive overhead that degrades both reasoning and extraction quality.
